label: early f/x inputs; <DEL> after sequences starting w/t/z/0/2
explanation: Diffuse unit made of several partial clauses, none dominant. (1) Original-phase inputs f or x, mostly at early positions (t<5); input f has the highest rate (28%) and x 24%. (2) The <DEL> step, where it fires most strongly (all top-12 activations are <DEL>), especially when the first original token is in {w,t,z,0,2} and L is short (rate 13% at L=3 vs 4% at L=9). (3) A weaker copy-phase component on steps that output w/0/t/z (w 35%). Inputs 1, 3, h are weakly enriched. It almost never fires late in the original phase (orig_idx>=5) or at recall_idx 1. The two-clause predicate reaches only dev F1 about 0.44 and mass recall about 0.46; adding a copy-phase output-w clause barely helps (F1 0.45). About half the activation mass is spread over context-dependent steps that no simple token or position rule captures.
